#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Load libraries and dataset

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)   
tidymodels_prefer()   


attrition <- read_csv("attrition.csv")   # load dataset

# response - Attrition
# features - all remaining variables

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data exploration and necessary cleaning

```{r}
# convert all character variables to factor variables

attrition <- attrition |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

```


```{r}

# relevel the levels of the ordinal categorical features

attrition$BusinessTravel <- factor(attrition$BusinessTravel, 
                            levels = c("Non-Travel", "Travel_Rarely", "Travel_Frequently"))

attrition$Education <- factor(attrition$Education, 
                            levels = c("Below_College", "College", "Bachelor", "Master", "Doctor"))

attrition$EnvironmentSatisfaction <- factor(attrition$EnvironmentSatisfaction,
                            levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Very_High"))

attrition$JobInvolvement <- factor(attrition$JobInvolvement,
                            levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Very_High"))

attrition$JobSatisfaction <- factor(attrition$JobSatisfaction,
                            levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Very_High"))

attrition$RelationshipSatisfaction <- factor(attrition$RelationshipSatisfaction,
                            levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Very_High"))

attrition$WorkLifeBalance <- factor(attrition$WorkLifeBalance,
                            levels = c("Bad", "Good", "Better", "Best"))

```


```{r}
# verify the levels of every factor

attrition |>
  select(where(is.factor)) |>
  map(levels)

```


```{r}
# make "Yes" (employee leaves) the first level, that is, the event of interest

attrition <- attrition |>
  mutate(Attrition = fct_relevel(Attrition, "Yes"))

levels(attrition$Attrition)

```


```{r}
# imbalanced dataset in terms of response classes

attrition |>
  count(Attrition) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data splitting

```{r}
# split original data into training (60%), validation (20%), and test (20%) sets
# stratify on the response so each set keeps the similar attrition rate

set.seed(208)

attrition_split <- initial_validation_split(data = attrition,
                                            prop = c(0.6, 0.2),
                                            strata = Attrition)

attrition_train <- training(attrition_split)        # training set
attrition_validation <- validation(attrition_split) # validation set
attrition_test <- testing(attrition_split)          # test set

```

```{r}
# DEMONSTRATION
# verify even distribution of response classes across the three sets

bind_rows(train = attrition_train,
          validation = attrition_validation,
          test = attrition_test,
          .id = "set") |>
  count(set, Attrition) |>
  group_by(set) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Feature engineering, part 1: the base blueprint

```{r}

blueprint_base <- recipe(Attrition ~ ., data = attrition_train) |>
  
  step_integer(BusinessTravel, Education, EnvironmentSatisfaction, JobInvolvement,
               JobSatisfaction, PerformanceRating, RelationshipSatisfaction,
               WorkLifeBalance) |>
  
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Feature engineering, part 2: creating and transforming variables

Before writing new steps, we look at the **training set only** for ideas. Exploring the full data set before splitting is a form of data leakage: patterns we "discover" in the test rows end up shaping the model.

```{r}
# idea 1: are recent hires more likely to leave?

attrition_train |>
  mutate(NewHire = YearsAtCompany <= 1) |>
  group_by(NewHire) |>
  summarize(n = n(), attrition_rate = mean(Attrition == "Yes"))

```


```{r}
# idea 2: does the effect of overtime depend on marital status? (an interaction)

attrition_train |>
  group_by(OverTime, MaritalStatus) |>
  summarize(n = n(), attrition_rate = mean(Attrition == "Yes"), .groups = "drop")

```


```{r}
# idea 3: is monthly income right-skewed?

ggplot(attrition_train, aes(x = MonthlyIncome)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30)

```


```{r}
# idea 4: are some categories very rare?

attrition_train |>
  count(EducationField) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  arrange(prop)

```



```{r}
# engineered blueprint: the base recipe plus new and transformed variables

blueprint_fe <- recipe(Attrition ~ ., data = attrition_train) |>

  # (1) create new variables from existing ones (computed row by row)
  step_mutate(
    NewHire = as.integer(YearsAtCompany <= 1),                       # flag: 1 if tenure <= 1 year
    PriorExperience = TotalWorkingYears - YearsAtCompany,            # years worked before joining
    AvgYearsPerCompany = TotalWorkingYears / (NumCompaniesWorked + 1), # job-hopping measure
    RoleTenureShare = YearsInCurrentRole / (YearsAtCompany + 1)      # share of tenure in current role
  ) |>

  # (2) log-transform right-skewed features (offset = 1 because YearsAtCompany can be 0)
  step_log(MonthlyIncome) |>
  step_log(YearsAtCompany, offset = 1) |>

  # (3) ordinal features to integers (as in the base blueprint)
  step_integer(BusinessTravel, Education, EnvironmentSatisfaction, JobInvolvement,
               JobSatisfaction, PerformanceRating, RelationshipSatisfaction,
               WorkLifeBalance) |>

  # (4) a safety net: a category never seen in training becomes "new" instead of NA
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>

  # (5) lump categories with < 3% of training rows into one level
  step_other(EducationField, JobRole, threshold = 0.03, other = "Rare") |>

  # (6) normalize, then dummy encode (as in the base blueprint)
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>

  # (7) interaction between overtime and marital status (needs the dummy columns)
  step_interact(terms = ~ starts_with("OverTime_"):starts_with("MaritalStatus_")) |>

  # (8) remove columns with a single value (e.g., the empty "new" dummies from step 4)
  step_zv(all_predictors())

```


```{r}
# DEMONSTRATION / CHECK
# peek at the engineered features on the training data

blueprint_fe |>
  prep() |>
  bake(new_data = NULL) |> 
  glimpse()
  
```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Model specifications and workflows

```{r}

# logistic regression
logistic_spec <- logistic_reg() |>
  set_engine("glm") |>
  set_mode("classification")

# KNN with K to be tuned
knn_spec <- nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune(), weight_func = "rectangular") |>
  set_engine("kknn") |>
  set_mode("classification")

```

```{r}
# bundle recipe + model into workflows

logistic_wf <- workflow() |>              # logistic regression, base blueprint
  add_recipe(blueprint_base) |>
  add_model(logistic_spec)

logistic_fe_wf <- logistic_wf |>          # logistic regression, engineered blueprint
  update_recipe(blueprint_fe)

knn_wf <- workflow() |>                   # KNN, base recipe
  add_recipe(blueprint_base) |>
  add_model(knn_spec)

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### CV: compare recipes and models

```{r}
# 5-fold CV specifications stratified on the imbalanced response

set.seed(208)

attrition_folds <- vfold_cv(attrition_train, v = 5, strata = Attrition)

# metrics to compute in each fold
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, yardstick::sensitivity, yardstick::specificity)

```


```{r}
# CV with logistic regression (nothing to tune, so fit_resamples())

logistic_cv <- fit_resamples(logistic_wf,
                             resamples = attrition_folds,
                             metrics = class_metrics)

collect_metrics(logistic_cv)

```


```{r}

logistic_fe_cv <- fit_resamples(logistic_fe_wf,
                                resamples = attrition_folds,
                                metrics = class_metrics)

collect_metrics(logistic_fe_cv)

```


```{r}
# CV with KNN (tune K over 1, 3, 5, 7, 9)

k_grid <- tibble(neighbors = seq(1, 10, by = 2))

knn_cv <- tune_grid(knn_wf,
                    resamples = attrition_folds,
                    grid = k_grid,
                    metrics = class_metrics)

collect_metrics(knn_cv)

```


```{r}

autoplot(knn_cv)

best_k <- select_best(knn_cv, metric = "roc_auc")
best_k

```


```{r}
# choose the workflow with the best CV AUC

chosen_wf <- _____________

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Adjust the cutoff (threshold)

```{r}
# fit the chosen workflow on the training set

chosen_fit <- fit(chosen_wf, data = attrition_train)

```


```{r}
# predictions on the validation set: augment() adds .pred_class, .pred_Yes, .pred_No

val_preds <- augment(chosen_fit, new_data = attrition_validation)

val_preds |>
  select(Attrition, .pred_class, .pred_Yes, .pred_No) |>
  head()

```


```{r}
# baseline: confusion matrix and metrics at the default 0.5 cutoff

conf_mat(val_preds, truth = Attrition, estimate = .pred_class)

thresh_metrics <- metric_set(accuracy, yardstick::sensitivity, yardstick::specificity, ppv)

thresh_metrics(val_preds, truth = Attrition, estimate = .pred_class)

```


```{r}
# ROC curve and AUC for the validation set

val_roc <- val_preds |>
  roc_curve(truth = Attrition, .pred_Yes)

autoplot(val_roc)

val_preds |>
  roc_auc(truth = Attrition, .pred_Yes)

```


```{r}
# every candidate cutoff with its sensitivity and specificity

val_roc

```

```{r}
# DEMONSTRATION
# how sensitivity and specificity trade off as the cutoff moves

val_roc |>
  filter(is.finite(.threshold)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(sensitivity, specificity),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .threshold, y = value, color = metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Cutoff on P(Attrition = Yes)", y = "Value", color = NULL)

```


```{r}
# option 1: the point on the ROC curve closest to the top-left corner (0, 1)

val_roc |>
  mutate(dist_topleft = sqrt((1 - sensitivity)^2 + (1 - specificity)^2)) |>
  slice_min(dist_topleft, n = 1)

```


```{r}
# option 2: "catch at least 80% of leavers"
# among cutoffs with sensitivity >= 0.80, take the one with the best specificity

val_roc |>
  filter(sensitivity >= 0.80) |>
  slice_max(specificity, n = 1)

```



```{r}
# set the cutoff 

threshold <- ________   

# class label predictions for validation set using the new cutoff
val_preds <- val_preds |>
  mutate(.pred_class_thresh = factor(if_else(.pred_Yes >= threshold, "Yes", "No"),
                                     levels = c("Yes", "No")))

# confusion matrix for validation set
conf_mat(val_preds, truth = Attrition, estimate = .pred_class_thresh)

```


```{r}
# DEMONSTRATION
# compare metrics: default 0.5 cutoff vs. new cutoff

bind_rows(
  default_0.5 = thresh_metrics(val_preds, truth = Attrition, estimate = .pred_class),
  new_cutoff = thresh_metrics(val_preds, truth = Attrition, estimate = .pred_class_thresh),
  .id = "cutoff"
) |>
  select(cutoff, .metric, .estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cutoff, values_from = .estimate)

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Final model and test set performance

```{r}
# last_fit(): refits the chosen workflow on training + validation (80% of the data)
# and evaluates it once on the test set

final_fit <- last_fit(chosen_wf,
                      split = attrition_split,
                      add_validation_set = TRUE,
                      metrics = metric_set(roc_auc))

```


```{r}
# test set probability predictions to class predictions with the chosen cutoff

test_preds <- collect_predictions(final_fit) |>
  mutate(.pred_class_thresh = factor(if_else(.pred_Yes >= threshold, "Yes", "No"),
                                     levels = c("Yes", "No")))

```


```{r}
# confusion matrix and metrics for the test set

conf_mat(test_preds, truth = Attrition, estimate = .pred_class_thresh)

thresh_metrics(test_preds, truth = Attrition, estimate = .pred_class_thresh)

```


```{r}
# ROC curve for the test set

test_preds |>
  roc_curve(truth = Attrition, .pred_Yes) |>
  autoplot()

```
